identity.name: Kingdom of Jiaodong (Eighteen Kingdoms)
alt_names: Kingdom of Jiaodong under Xiang Yu

land.text: eastern Shandong, one of the 'Three Qis' cut from the former Qi state

predecessors.note: Tian Rong page: Xiang Yu 'divided Qi into Qi, Jiaodong, and Jibei, appointing Tian Du, Tian Fu, and Tian An as kings'; the Eighteen Kingdoms page: they 'occupied the area of the former Qi state'.

successors.note: Eighteen Kingdoms page: 'Tian Rong conquered Jiaodong and Jibei, reuniting the old Qi state'.

capitals.name: Jimo (ancient site in Pingdu, Shandong)
capitals.note: The Jiaodong Kingdom page gives 'its capital in Jimo (the site is in today's Pingdu, not Jimo, Shandong)' for the Han-dynasty kingdom of that name, not for Tian Fu's; unverified for 206. Coordinates are Pingdu's (places.jsonl); the ancient site is within about 30 km.

rulers.name: Tian Fu (Tian Shi)
rulers.note: The Eighteen Kingdoms, Tian Rong and Timeline pages say Tian Fu; the Chu-Han Contention page calls the king of Jiaodong 'Tian Shi'.

correction.text: unchanged outline, but only for 206: Tian Rong conquered the kingdom and killed its king in that year

keyframe_review.note: 51,055 km2, bbox 118.0-122.7 E, 35.5-37.9 N: the table's 'eastern Shandong'. No page opened gives an area, so no infobox figure to compare. Cliopatria keeps the row to 204; the Timeline page puts Tian Rong's conquest under 206 BC and the Chu-Han page 'six months after Qin dynasty's collapse', so the cells belong to Qi (Tian Rong) from 206. The Tian Rong page says 205; see ledger.

region.text: eastern Shandong (Eighteen Kingdoms table), cut from the old Qi for Tian Fu

ledger.note: 206: Xiang Yu cuts Jiaodong from Qi and makes Tian Fu its king. 'he divided Qi into Qi, Jiaodong, and Jibei, appointing Tian Du, Tian Fu, and Tian An as kings'; the Eighteen Kingdoms table: 'Jiaodong (膠東): Tian Fu (Qi royalty); eastern Shandong'. The Xiang Yu page dates the division 'In the spring of 206 BC'.

region.text: eastern Shandong (Eighteen Kingdoms table), cut from the old Qi for Tian Fu

ledger.note: 206: Tian Rong conquers Jiaodong and kills its king. 'Tian Rong conquers the Kingdom of Jiaodong and kills its king, Tian Fu.' The Chu-Han Contention page: 'Merely six months after Qin dynasty's collapse' Tian Rong 'killed Tian Shi, the King of Jiaodong, and Tian An, the King of Jibei'; the Tian Rong page dates the killing to 205 ('When Liu Bang's anti-Chu coalition rose in 205 BC, Tian Rong revolted'). 206 is used (two pages); the month is on none.

region.text: eastern Shandong (Eighteen Kingdoms table), cut from the old Qi for Tian Fu

ledger.note: 206: the Kingdom of Jiaodong ends and Tian Rong's Qi holds eastern Shandong. 'Tian Rong conquered Jiaodong and Jibei, reuniting the old Qi state' (Eighteen Kingdoms page, undated). Date as for the loss.

wars.name: Revolt of Tian Rong against the Three Qis
wars.outcome: Qi (Tian Rong) victory: 'Tian Rong conquers the Kingdom of Jiaodong and kills its king, Tian Fu' (Timeline, 206 BC); Jiaodong and Jibei were reunited with Qi. Xiang Yu 'counter-attacked, retaking Linzi' late in 205 (Tian Rong page).
wars.note: The month and the place of Tian Fu's death are on no page opened; the Tian Rong page does not mention Jimo in this context. Reviewer 2026-10-19: renamed from 'Chu–Han Contention' (206-202) to the qi dossier's name for this war, 206 only, to pair with qi and jibei.

certainty.note: The kingdom was assigned by Xiang Yu from the old Qi; no survey or treaty lines; the outline is Cliopatria's approximation.

sources.title: Eighteen Kingdoms
sources.note: Table row for Jiaodong: Tian Fu (Qi royalty), eastern Shandong; 'Tian Rong conquered Jiaodong and Jibei' (undated).

sources.title: Tian Rong
sources.note: Xiang Yu divides Qi into three; Tian Rong's revolt dated 205 on this page.

sources.title: Jiaodong Kingdom
sources.note: Capital Jimo (Pingdu site) of the Han-dynasty kingdom; thin for 206.

sources.title: Timeline of the Chu–Han Contention
sources.note: 206 BC entries: Tian Rong conquers Jiaodong and kills Tian Fu.

sources.title: Chu–Han Contention

notes:
Wikidata Q5349053 is the Eighteen Kingdoms item shared by twelve Cliopatria rows; Jiaodong is its own kingdom (Tian Fu), so it keeps its own dossier. The later Han-dynasty Jiaodong Kingdom (148 BC onward, Jiaodong Kingdom page) is another entity and not in Cliopatria.
Date conflict: Tian Rong page 205, Timeline and Chu-Han Contention pages 206 (or 'six months after' the collapse). 206 is used and matches the jibei dossier (ea-02-a), which records Tian An's death and the loss to Qi in 206.
The qi dossier (ea-01) has no gain from jiaodong or jibei, and Cliopatria's Qi row (60,204 km2, central and western Shandong) does not cover eastern Shandong; the compiler needs Qi's gain of the Jiaodong cells in 206 or the cells fall to grey. The Cliopatria row runs to 204 and is cut to 206 here.
Tian Fu and Tian Shi are the same man (the Chu-Han Contention page uses Tian Shi). Capital: see the capital note.
